enforcement_note: Nothing can enforce this. No hook can tell a tested claim from a confident one - both arrive as ordinary assistant text, and the dispatcher sees tool calls, not assertions. A PostToolUse hook could count executions but not tell which claim they settled. What exists is indirect: the loop detector notices repeated identical calls, which is the shape of arguing rather than testing. Enforcement would require a judge of claim-to-evidence linkage, which this repository has no way to build stdlib-only.
maps_to_v14_step_reason: No v14 ancestor. Self-hardened locally on 2026-08-06 after a planning session in which a vendored guide and this repository's own skill disagreed about whether the Stop hook can block. Two rounds of citation settled nothing; executing the hook settled it in one command. Recorded in history/2026-W32.md.
rule: When a factual claim about system behaviour is disputed or uncertain, test it directly. Test every competing claim, not only the one you expect to win.
condition: A claim about how the system behaves is contradicted, unverified, or resting on documentation alone.
ai_action: Design the test from the documentation, then run it - never cite documentation in place of executing. Test each competing claim, including your own, and report the raw output rather than a paraphrase. If a claim genuinely cannot be executed, label it unproven and say what evidence would settle it; do not promote the best-argued position to a conclusion. When settling it needs the user, write the instructions in plain language: exactly what to do, what a pass looks like, what a failure looks like, and why it cannot be done without them. Assume no expertise - no jargon, no 'simply run', no assuming familiarity with hooks, stdin, or the tool surface.

provenance.source: self-hardened from a recorded planning failure
